note: AI preparation for BUILD_PLAN 2.3: one analyst and one adversarial checker per event (plus a fix round on blocking defects). Evidence for the owner's sign-off, not the sign-off itself.

accepted_warnings.reason: This is the true sink, recorded as the sink's true_symbol. With its overloads it is about 16 KB, which would push the clean slice to about 36 KB, well over the 24 KB soft limit. Git._call_process, the stand-in, shows the self.execute(call) call site.

analyst.class_note: Matches the advisory label (CWE-78/CWE-184). The mechanism is argument injection into git's argv: an abbreviated option such as --upload-p is expanded by git to --upload-pack. The injected option makes git run the caller-supplied value as a program, so the impact is OS command execution. I checked this with git 2.55.0.windows.3: `git clone --upload-p='touch MARKER; false' <local bare repo> out` created the marker.
concerns: The sink is recorded as a stand-in: Git.execute, which holds the literal Popen/safer_popen call, is not in the slice. Tools that need to see the subprocess call itself (Pysa, Semgrep, Bandit) will only see an opaque self.execute(call) in _call_process. The true_symbol records the real location, but gate results on this event depend on how each gate handles an unresolved callee.

The tainted datum is a kwarg KEY (the option name), not only its value. Taint engines that propagate only dict values, or that do not model **kwargs keys flowing into f-string argv construction in transform_kwarg, may miss the flow in both variants.

The fix is known-incomplete: the residual bypass with an extra '-': False kwarg exists at the clean commit, and upstream closes it only in 701ce32f (GHSA-956x-8gvw-wg5v). The modelled flow is closed, but the clean slice is not fully safe against the advisory's broader weakness.

The clean check_unsafe_options keeps the fix's own 6-line comment, which says an abbreviated spelling such as --upl for --upload-pack 'must be rejected too'. The scrubber did not flag it: its wording matches real identifiers (unsafe_options, UnsafeOptionError, 'blocked'), and it contains no vulnerability/CVE/security terms. Its deletion does appear in regression.diff, which gives a diff-only gate a lexical hint. That is inherent to the real fix.

The slicer drops attribute docstrings in both variants, including the unsafe_git_clone_options docstring ('Options ... that allow arbitrary commands to be executed'). That drop is not listed under 'scrubbed' in event.json. It is harmless here because both variants lose it, but the scrubbed log does not fully describe what was removed.

Some names are referenced in the slice but not defined in it: base.py calls Git.check_unsafe_protocols, Git.polish_url and Git.is_cygwin, and Git's metaclass _GitMeta is also undefined in the slice. None of these are on the flow. A model rewriting cmd.py whole might try to fill them in.

The pair (b920dcd4 -> 181e8ede) is settled and correct for the prefix-abbreviation bug. The advisory itself links 56806080, the joined-short-option fix, which is event gitpython-v396, so this pair deliberately ends one commit earlier. regression.diff contains only the inverted check_unsafe_options change, with no unrelated hunks.
analyst.fix_effect_note: The clean commit closes the modelled flow: the plain upload_p kwarg from the advisory's PoC, plus upload_pac, conf and multi_options '--upl=...'. The fix is known-incomplete. At 181e8ede, adding an extra kwarg key that starts with '-' and has the value False or None (for example **{'upload_p': prog, '-': False}) makes options_are_kwargs False. That switches off prefix matching for every kwarg, and the '-' key produces no argv, so --upload-p=prog still reaches git. I confirmed this bypass against the extracted clean guard. It survives 56806080 (options_are_kwargs is unchanged there). Upstream closes it only in 701ce32f (GHSA-956x-8gvw-wg5v), where _clone switches to Git._option_candidates([], kwargs); that drops False/None keys and spells multi-character kwargs as --long options. This is recorded in the spec notes.
analyst.flow_summary: Entry: git/repo/base.py::Repo.clone_from is a library API. It forwards the caller's **kwargs unchanged (for example upload_p=<program>) to Repo._clone. Guard: _clone calls git/cmd.py::Git.check_unsafe_options(options=list(kwargs.keys()), unsafe_options=Repo.unsafe_git_clone_options). At the regressed commit b920dcd4 the guard canonicalises only '_'->'-' and does an exact dict lookup, so 'upload-p' misses '--upload-pack' and the call passes. At the clean commit 181e8ede it also rejects any --long option or multi-character kwarg whose canonical name is a prefix of a blocked option, so upload_p is refused. Path to the sink: _clone calls git.clone(multi, '--', url, path, ..., **add_progress(kwargs, ...)), and add_progress only adds progress=True. git.clone resolves through Git.__getattr__ to a lambda that calls Git._call_process. There transform_kwargs/transform_kwarg emit '--upload-p=<program>' and self.execute(call) runs it. Sink: git/cmd.py::Git._call_process stands in for git/cmd.py::Git.execute, where safer_popen/Popen starts git. git expands --upload-p to --upload-pack and runs <program>. I extracted the guard at both commits and tested it. At b920dcd4 it passes upload_p, upload_pac, conf and '--upl=x'. At 181e8ede it blocks all four. The exact forms upload_pack and u are blocked at both commits. The multi_options path (['--upl=<prog>'] -> shlex split -> check_unsafe_options -> _unpack_args -> _call_process) runs through the same symbols and is closed the same way.
analyst.scope_evidence: The entry Repo.clone_from, and the _clone call site that calls the guard, are in git/repo/base.py. The guard Git.check_unsafe_options is in git/cmd.py, which is the only file the regression changes. The stand-in sink Git._call_process and the true sink Git.execute are also in git/cmd.py. Entry and guard/sink are in different files, so the build computes cross_file. The true_symbol is in the same file as its stand-in, so it does not affect the label.

Repo.clone_from(**kwargs) calls cls._clone(..., **kwargs) (base.py:274). _clone calls Git.check_unsafe_options(options=list(kwargs.keys()), ...) (base.py:174), which in cmd.py:151-159 does only an exact canonical dict lookup. Then git.clone(multi, '--', ..., **add_progress(kwargs, git, progress)) goes to Git.__getattr__ (cmd.py:165), which returns a lambda calling _call_process. _call_process calls transform_kwargs and transform_kwarg, which emit '--upload-p=<value>' (cmd.py:189), then self.execute(call) (cmd.py:310). add_progress is not in the slice. The real repo at b920dcd4 has no other option filtering on this path: grep of cmd.py, repo/base.py and remote.py finds only check_unsafe_options and check_unsafe_protocols. I extracted the slice's own check_unsafe_options and transform_kwargs and ran them. At regressed, upload_p, upload_pac, conf, up, '--upl=x' and ['depth','upload_p'] all PASS. transform_kwargs(upload_p='touch X; false') yields ['--upload-p=touch X; false'].

analyst.class_note: Same as the advisory label (CWE-22, also CWE-73). The class is chosen by impact: the caller picks the directory that git checkout-index writes into, which gives an arbitrary file overwrite outside the work tree. The mechanism is option injection into git's argv (CWE-88 style), so 'command' (CWE-77) is a possible alternative reading. The GitPython events are labelled by impact throughout (gitpython-2f96 is os-command), so path-traversal keeps this one consistent.
concerns: The fix is known to be incomplete. Its other half, TagReference.create (git tag -F/--file, arbitrary read), was bypassed at the clean commit through positional reference='--file=<path>' and joined short options, and was fixed later by GHSA-3wxw-xv34-2frg / 1b0d2d9b and GHSA-wvpp-8hx9-p66j / 96a888f4. That half is deliberately left out: git/refs/tag.py is not in the slice, and regression.diff contains only the 4 IndexFile.checkout hunks (the class attribute, the parameter, its docstring lines, and the guard call). There are no unrelated hunks.

Scope is disputed. Rule-based scope is cross_file because the Popen and the kwargs-to-argv transform are in git/cmd.py. The 2.2 confirm reviewer called it local. If the owner instead treats the repo.git.checkout_index(...) 'git invocation' inside IndexFile.checkout as the sink, the label would be local. I kept the sink convention of gitpython-2f96 (Git._call_process, with true_symbol Git.execute).

The hop self.repo.git.checkout_index -> Git.__getattr__ -> Git._call_process is dynamic dispatch through Repo.git (git/repo/base.py, not sliced; IndexFile.__init__, which types self.repo, is also cut). A static call-graph gate will likely record an unknown edge here rather than a resolved one, so the cross-file flow depends on how the gate handles __getattr__ dispatch.
The tainted datum is a kwarg KEY (the option name) as well as its value. Taint engines that only propagate values, possibly Pysa or Semgrep, may miss the source->sink link.

The slice's cmd.py contains the project's own vocabulary 'unsafe' in identifiers and messages (check_unsafe_options, UnsafeOptionError, unsafe_git_ls_remote_options, re_unsafe_protocol, the 'unsafe-option checks' docstring), and it is identical in both variants. The clean base.py adds the real fix's docstring line 'Allow unsafe options, such as ``--prefix``.' This is all real code, not injected framing, and the flagged-strings check is clean. Still, the regressed slice shows the guard helper in cmd.py, which could nudge a rewriting model to restore the guard unprompted. The scrubber removed 2 security-worded comments or docstring paragraphs from cmd.py in each variant.

At 24533 bytes, the clean slice is 43 bytes under the 24 KB soft limit. execute_kwargs and Git._unpack_args (both referenced by Git._call_process) were cut to fit, so those two names are undefined in the slice.

Not closed by this commit, and not an option-injection flow, so not modelled: IndexFile.checkout(env={'GIT_WORK_TREE': <dir>}) is an execute kwarg that Git.execute merges into the child environment. I confirmed with git 2.55 that git checkout-index --index --force --all then writes into <dir>. The clean slice is therefore not free of every outside-the-repo write channel, though a gate built on injection rules should not flag it.

spec.json is the pilot spec, kept after critical review. On 2026-09-28 I only extended its notes (the class rationale, re-verification results, the separate-token '--prefix <string>' form being unreachable, and the @default_index decorator being off-flow). Flow, slice and class are unchanged, and I edited no built files by hand.
analyst.fix_effect_note: Commit 3af0c251 guards two call sites. The TagReference.create (git tag -F/--file) guard is incomplete at this commit: the positional reference/path bypass and joined short options were fixed later by GHSA-3wxw-xv34-2frg / 1b0d2d9b and GHSA-wvpp / 96a888f4. The extracted flow, IndexFile.checkout kwargs -> git checkout-index --prefix, is fully closed; I verified this myself on 2026-09-28 with real git 2.55.0.windows.3 and GitPython's own helpers extracted from git/cmd.py (whose blob is identical at both commits). With the guard absent, each of prefix=, pre=, prefi=, u='--prefix=...' (split), prefix=[...] and the key form 'prefix=<dir>/' reached git (rc 0) and wrote or overwrote f.txt outside the repo. With the clean guard, every one of them raises UnsafeOptionError, and a harmless q=True still passes. The spellings the guard lets through never reach the option: u='--prefix=...' with split_single_char_options=False becomes '-u--prefix=...', and p=<dir> becomes '-p <dir>'; git rejects both with rc 129. --prefix has no short form, positional args are fixed, and explicit paths go over stdin.
analyst.flow_summary: The flow starts at git/index/base.py::IndexFile.checkout, a public library API that takes the caller's **kwargs, e.g. index.checkout(prefix='/abs/dir/', force=True). In the regressed commit there is no guard. With paths=None the method builds args ['--index', '--force', '--all'], sets kwargs['as_process']=1 and calls self.repo.git.checkout_index(*args, **kwargs). That call dispatches dynamically through Repo.git and Git.__getattr__ in git/cmd.py to Git._call_process. There, the execute_kwargs membership test separates as_process from the option kwargs. transform_kwargs and transform_kwarg then turn prefix=<dir> into '--prefix=<dir>', and self.execute(call) starts 'git checkout-index --prefix=<dir> --index --force --all'. The real Popen (via safer_popen) is inside Git.execute, about 350 lines long; it is recorded as true_symbol, and Git._call_process is the sink symbol kept in the slice. git then writes every indexed blob under the caller's path and overwrites existing files. In the clean commit, IndexFile.checkout adds allow_unsafe_options=False and runs Git.check_unsafe_options(Git._option_candidates([], kwargs), unsafe_git_checkout_index_options=['--prefix']) before building args. That raises UnsafeOptionError for prefix=, the abbreviations pre= and prefi=, a list value, the key form 'prefix=<dir>/', and the split form u='--prefix=<dir>'. The fix is known to be incomplete, but only in its TagReference.create half: positional reference='--file=...' and clustered short options were bypassed, and those gaps were closed later by GHSA-3wxw (1b0d2d9b) and GHSA-wvpp (96a888f4). This event models only the checkout-index kwargs path, which this commit does fully close. git/refs/tag.py is left out of the slice, so regression.diff carries only the checkout hunks.
analyst.scope_evidence: Entry (IndexFile.checkout) and guard (the check added to IndexFile.checkout) are both in git/index/base.py, the only file the regression changes. The true sink is git/cmd.py::Git.execute, where the subprocess starts. The kwargs-to-'--prefix=' transformation happens in git/cmd.py too (Git._call_process / transform_kwarg, with Git._call_process as the in-slice stand-in). So the pre-registered rule gives cross_file; the built event.json says scope=cross_file. The 2.2 reviewers disagreed (confirm said local, refute said cross-file). Treating the repo.git.checkout_index(...) call inside IndexFile.checkout as the sink would make it local, but gitpython-2f96 uses Git._call_process/Git.execute as the sink for the same dispatch path, and the scope was not picked by choosing a stand-in.

check.class_note: The advisory CWEs are CWE-22, CWE-73 and CWE-200, and the impact is a caller-chosen output directory for git checkout-index (arbitrary file write), so path-traversal is right. 'command' (CWE-77/88, option injection) is a defensible alternative reading of the mechanism. The dossier says so, and labelling by impact is consistent with the other GitPython events.
check.clean_blocks_note: In clean/, the guard runs at the top of IndexFile.checkout, before either branch, so it sits on the same path. I extracted GitPython's real helpers from the cmd.py blob and ran the guard against these payloads. It raised UnsafeOptionError for: prefix=, pre=, prefix=[...], prefix=0, a set value, the key 'prefix=/x/', the key 'prefix\t', u='--prefix=...', f='--prefix=...', u=('--prefix=...',) and u=['-q','--prefix=...']. It let through: p=<dir> ('-p <dir>'), PREFIX=, u='--prefix=...' with split_single_char_options=False ('-u--prefix=...'), stage='all --prefix=/x' (a single token), x='y --prefix=/x', u=' --prefix=/x/', and q=True. I ran the passing spellings against real git: -p, -u--prefix=... and --PREFIX= all exit 129, and the leading-space operand is fatal ("don't mix '--all' and explicit filenames"). None of the passes reaches the option, so this flow (the kwargs path to --prefix) is closed. The known incompleteness is on the TagReference.create half only (GHSA-3wxw, GHSA-wvpp), and that half is correctly left out. The env={'GIT_WORK_TREE':...} channel is outside this option-injection flow and is disclosed in the notes.

analyst.class_note: Matches the advisory label (CWE-78). Strictly this is option/argument injection (CWE-88): the caller controls a git option name, and its effect is that git runs a hook, so the command execution is real OS command execution. It is not CWE-77 in the sense of injecting shell or command text.
concerns: The clean slice keeps the fix's own comment above the new list entry: '# Can install hooks that execute during clone:'. It does not match the scrubber's pattern and it states git behaviour, not security framing. Still, the scrubber removed the older entries' comments ('Executes arbitrary commands:' and similar), so this is the only per-entry comment left in unsafe_git_clone_options. It explains why the entry exists, and it appears in regression.diff as part of the inverted fix. The only way to remove it would be a scrubber rule change, not a spec edit; the owner should decide.

git/remote.py::add_progress, an identity passthrough for the kwargs dict that adds only progress=True, is cut from the slice. The tainted kwargs pass through it on the way to git.clone. The attack is less powerful than the advisory claims. With git 2.55, git refuses a --separate-git-dir whose parent directory does not exist ('Invalid path'). The advisory's 'silently populates/overwrites another repository's .git' did not reproduce, and hook execution would need a later git command, which is outside this flow. analyst.class_note: Matches the advisory label (CWE-77/CWE-88). Judged by the code: GitPython builds a git argv list with no shell, and caller-chosen kwarg names become git options placed before '--'. That is argument injection (CWE-88, a child of CWE-77). The injected --exec makes git start a caller-chosen program, so the effect is command execution. Sibling events with the same mechanism (gitpython-2f96 and others) are labelled os-command because their advisories say CWE-78. The mechanism fits either label; the owner may want to make these consistent.

analyst.flow_summary:
Entry: git/repo/base.py::Repo.commit(rev), a public library API. It calls self.rev_parse(str(rev) + '^0'). Repo.rev_parse is a class-level alias of git/repo/fun.py::rev_parse. rev_parse passes the text before the first '^' to name_to_object('/etc/passwd'). name_to_object tries the bare '%s' template first and calls SymbolicReference.dereference_recursive(repo, '/etc/passwd'), which goes through _get_ref_info to _get_ref_info_helper in git/refs/symbolic.py. That is the sink: open(os.path.join(_git_dir(repo, ref_path), str(ref_path))). Because the path is absolute, os.path.join throws away repodir, so the file is opened and read in full.

Guard: at the regressed commit 1774f1e3 the only check is `if '..' in str(ref_path): raise ValueError`. This is the first, incomplete fix 74e55ee4, so an absolute name still reaches the sink. At the clean commit e98f57b8, _get_ref_info_helper first calls the new SymbolicReference._check_ref_name_valid, which applies the git-check-ref-format rules. It rejects a leading '/' (and '//' for the 'refs/%s' templates, which also blocks those). Every template therefore raises ValueError, and name_to_object ends in BadName without opening anything.

Verified on 2026-09-29. I extracted the complete git/ package at each commit, stubbed only the external gitdb and smmap, and called Repo.commit against a real temporary repo while an audit hook logged every open(). Results:
- 1774f1e3: an absolute rev opened a marker file outside .git.
- e98f57b8: the same rev opened nothing.
- '../x' was rejected at both commits without any open.
- 'master' produced the same opens inside .git at both commits.
analyst.scope_evidence: The entry, Repo.commit, is in git/repo/base.py. The guard (SymbolicReference._check_ref_name_valid, called from _get_ref_info_helper) and the sink (SymbolicReference._get_ref_info_helper, which runs open(os.path.join(...))) are both in git/refs/symbolic.py. The flow goes from one to the other through git/repo/fun.py (rev_parse, then name_to_object). The entry is the real public API function, not a stand-in, and no true_symbol is needed. Because the entry and the sink are in different files, the built event.json has scope=cross_file (flow_files: git/refs/symbolic.py, git/repo/base.py).

check.clean_blocks_note:
In clean/, _get_ref_info_helper runs `if ref_path: cls._check_ref_name_valid(ref_path)` before _git_dir and open. This is on the same path and is byte-identical to the real e98f57b8 code. I traced the concrete payload Repo.commit('/etc/passwd') through each template name_to_object tries:
- '/etc/passwd': the first character is '/' with previous None, so it raises "cannot start with forward slashes".
- 'refs//etc/passwd', 'refs/tags//etc/passwd', 'refs/heads//etc/passwd', 'refs/remotes//etc/passwd' and 'refs/remotes//etc/passwd/HEAD': each contains '//' and raises.

Every one of these raises ValueError, and name_to_object catches it (fun.py:81). hexsha stays None, BadName is raised, and open() is never reached. Backslash (Windows-style) paths and '..' are also rejected. The fix is only the second half of a two-part fix, but the recorded flow, the absolute-path variant, is closed on this pair and open on the regressed side, so the pair discriminates correctly.

analyst.class_note: The class matches the advisory's CWE-22 label. The code confirms it: a submodule name such as '../../../escaped/module' from .gitmodules is joined unnormalised into <git_dir>/modules/<name>. That lets os.makedirs and git clone --separate-git-dir write outside the repository.
concerns: Scope depends on where the sink is taken. The spec records Submodule._clone_repo (os.makedirs) as the sink, which gives local. If the git clone --separate-git-dir subprocess (Repo.clone_from in git/repo/base.py, then Git.execute in git/cmd.py) were treated as the true sink, the label would be cross_file. The 2.2 reviewers also split on scope, local versus cross-file.

Clean-side robustness bug that a gate or model may notice. At e4b8e7d0, update(recursive=True, keep_going=True) on a rejected name logs the ValueError and then reads mrepo while it is unbound, raising UnboundLocalError. mrepo is only initialised under dry_run. Follow-up b324c831 fixes this; it does not affect the guard.

Two candidate fix commits were flagged at 2.2. The second one, 4299c990, moves validation ahead of the git-version branch in _module_abspath. It is consistency hardening on the legacy branch, which uses path rather than name, and is not needed to close the modelled flow. The clean commit closes the flow on its own.

The slice keeps the real docstrings of _clone_repo and update, including 'Allow unsafe options/protocols to be used, like --upload-pack / ext'. These are the library's own API docs for its allow_unsafe_* parameters, unrelated to the name flow, and the scrubber did not remove them. I judged them not revealing, but the owner may want to know they are there.
The clean slice is 24,216 bytes, just under the 24,576-byte soft limit. There is no room to add Submodule.module or _config_parser without a size WARN.
To trigger the flow, the .gitmodules path entry must still name a real gitlink so that iter_items yields the submodule. Only the name has to be malicious, as in the fix's own test.
analyst.fix_effect_note:
In the clean commit, update validates self.name before the module lookup, reconnect or clone, and _module_abspath validates on the gitfile branch. Both the clone path and the reconnect path therefore raise ValueError before any filesystem operation.

The follow-up 4299c990 only moves the check ahead of the git-version branch in _module_abspath. The legacy branch (git < 1.7.5) joins path, not name, so it is not needed to close this flow. The other follow-up, b324c831, fixes an unbound mrepo on update(recursive=True, keep_going=True). That is robustness, not part of the guard.

The fix also guards add, move, remove, rename and module(). These are parallel sites the slice leaves out, so their hunks are not in regression.diff.
analyst.flow_summary:
Regressed commit 6e61b1d3, all in git/objects/submodule/base.py:
1. Entry: Submodule.iter_items reads each section header of the cloned repository's .gitmodules through parser.sections(). It passes the header to sm_name() in util.py, which only strips the 'submodule "..."' wrapper, and stores the result unchecked as sm._name. The Submodule.name property returns it.
2. The caller runs sm.update(init=True), or Repo.submodule_update, which reaches it through RootModule.update.
3. In update, self.module() raises InvalidGitRepositoryError. update then calls module_abspath = self._module_abspath(self.repo, self.path, self.name). On git >= 1.7.5 this is osp.join(git_dir, 'modules', name), with no normalisation.
4. No repository exists at that path, so update calls self._clone_repo(self.repo, url, self.path, self.name, ...).
5. Sink: _clone_repo recomputes _module_abspath and calls os.makedirs(osp.dirname(module_abspath)). It also sets separate_git_dir=module_abspath for git.Repo.clone_from, so git clone --separate-git-dir creates a full repository outside the clone. separate-git-dir is not in unsafe_git_clone_options at either commit.
6. A second path in the same slice: update's reconnect branch calls _write_git_file_and_module_config on a repository that already exists at the escaped path.

Guards at clean commit e4b8e7d0:
- The new Submodule._validated_name rejects an empty name, a leading / or \, a drive-qualified name, and any '..' component under either separator.
- _module_abspath now joins cls._validated_name(name) on the gitfile branch.
- update calls self._validated_name(self.name) first inside its try block, so a ValueError is raised before any path is built.

Re-checked with the functions extracted from each commit. The regressed makedirs created <parent-of-clone>/escaped. The clean guard raised ValueError for the same name and for '..', '../m', 'a/../../m', '/abs/m', '\m', 'C:m' and 'a\..\..\m', while accepting 'module' and 'lib/sub'.

- Sink: Submodule._clone_repo, which contains os.makedirs(osp.dirname(module_abspath)), the first dangerous call that receives the tainted path.

The 2.2 reviewers split on scope. The confirming reviewer said local; the refuting reviewer said cross-file, treating sm_name as the source. The spec follows the local reading.

A reader who records the git clone subprocess, which runs through Repo.clone_from (git/repo/base.py) and Git.execute (git/cmd.py), as the true sink would get cross_file instead. The spec's notes say this explicitly.

analyst.class_note: Same as the advisory label (CWE-78) and the finished gitpython-2f96 example. Strictly, the mechanism is argument injection into git's argv (Git.execute uses Popen with shell=False by default). The injected -u/--upload-pack option then makes git run the caller's value as a shell command, so the impact is OS command execution. The owner may want to say "CWE-88 mechanism, CWE-78 impact" in the write-up.
concerns: The class body kept in the built git/repo/base.py (both variants) still has class-level assignments that name methods cut from the slice: `description = property(_get_description, _set_description, ...)`, `refs = references`, `branches = heads`, `daemon_export = property(_get_daemon_export, ...)`, `alternates = property(_get_alternates, ...)`. The slice parses, but these names are undefined in the class body, and the builder's dropped-references check does not report them. gitpython-cwvm has the same leftover. A code-generation model that rewrites the file whole might 'fix' or delete these lines, which would add spurious diffs to the trace. Adding the 8 methods would cost ~2.6 KB and take the clean slice to ~23.6 KB (soft limit 24 KB). I left them out because they are off-flow; a builder-level fix (flag or drop such assignments) would fix this for every event.

Two cosmetic results of scrubbing: in unsafe_git_clone_options the comment '# Users can override configuration variables' is left as a fragment (its second line, which mentioned executing arbitrary commands, was removed), and check_unsafe_options keeps only 'Check for unsafe options.' as its docstring. Real identifiers and API docstrings still say 'unsafe' (allow_unsafe_options, UnsafeOptionError, unsafe_git_clone_options, and ':param allow_unsafe_options: Allow unsafe options to be used, like --upload-pack'). That is real program behaviour and documentation, so it stays, but it does tell the model which options are dangerous.

The tainted value that matters is a kwarg KEY (the option name), not only its value. Value-only taint engines (possibly Pysa) may see the value reach argv but not the option name that makes it dangerous, so baseline recall on this event may reflect that modelling limit rather than the gate.

The c=/config= variants are also blocked by the fix, but exploiting them needs a second ingredient (for example protocol.ext.allow=always plus an ext:: URL, which check_unsafe_protocols blocks by default). The modelled flow is therefore u=/upload-pack=<program>.

The fix commit is a merge (PR #1609). Its first-parent diff equals the PR's only commit 5c59e0d6 and touches only git/repo/base.py (+2 lines) plus tests, so regression.diff contains only the inverted 2-line guard. There are no unrelated hunks.

analyst.flow_summary: Entry: the public library API git/repo/base.py::Repo.clone_from(url, to_path, ..., **kwargs), and also Repo.clone(path, ..., **kwargs), which clones from self.common_dir. Both forward the caller's **kwargs unchanged to Repo._clone. There transform_kwargs/transform_kwarg turn u=PROG into ['-u', 'PROG'] (and upload-pack=PROG into '--upload-pack=PROG'), and self.execute(call) runs `git clone -v -u PROG -- <url> <path>` through Popen in Git.execute (the true sink, ~14 KB, cut from the slice; Git._call_process is the in-slice stand-in). git then runs PROG through the shell as its upload-pack. I re-ran two checks. First, the guard code taken from both built slices: at the regressed commit all four keys pass (u -> ['-u','PROG']), and at the clean commit all four are blocked. Second, real git 2.55 `git clone -v -u "touch MARKER; git-upload-pack" -- src.git dst` created MARKER.

analyst.class_note: Matches the advisory label (CWE-78/CWE-88). The mechanism is argument injection into git's argv, but the injected --upload-pack makes git run the caller's string as a shell command, so the effect is OS command execution. I confirmed this end to end with local git 2.55.0.windows.3: a marker file was created.
concerns:
Security-flavoured wording the scrubber does not catch: 'unsafe' and 'caller-controlled' are not in its REVEALING regex, so this text stays in both slices. None of it names a vulnerability, but it points at --upload-pack as dangerous. It all comes from the real API, and gitpython-2f96 has the same text. The model-visible items are:
- Real API identifiers: check_unsafe_options, UnsafeOptionError, allow_unsafe_options, unsafe_git_clone_options, unsafe_git_ls_remote_options.
- The Repo.clone_from docstring line 'Allow unsafe options to be used, like ``--upload-pack``.'
- The _canonicalize_option_name docstring 'Return the option name used for unsafe-option checks.'
- The class-level comment '# Writes output to a caller-controlled filesystem path.' in Repo.unsafe_git_archive_options.

One hop is outside the slice. Repo._clone passes the tainted kwargs as **add_progress(kwargs, git, progress). add_progress, in git/remote.py, returns the same dict and at most sets progress=True, but it is imported, not sliced. Adding it takes the clean slice to 24,677 bytes, just over the soft limit, and gitpython-2f96 leaves it out too. A taint engine without a pass-through model for it, or without dict and **kwargs field taint, may lose the flow at this call.
The true sink, Git.execute (safer_popen/Popen), is not in the slice. Gates that need a literal subprocess call will only see self.execute(call) in Git._call_process.

Whether the value is dangerous depends on its key: the smuggled token only runs when the one-letter key is a flag that takes no value (n and the other clusterable flags). After a flag that takes a value, such as b, git takes the token as that flag's value. Because of this dependence on the key, analysis that tracks values only may over- or under-approximate.

The sliced cmd.py has undefined names: _GitMeta in the class header and the TypeAlias targets _AutoInterrupt and _CatFileContentStream. A linter-style gate may flag them, and the code-generation model may try to 'fix' them. This is accepted, and consistent with gitpython-2f96.

The existing pilot notes wrongly said gitpython-2f96 used Repo._clone as its sink stand-in; 2f96 actually uses Git._call_process with true_symbol Git.execute. I corrected this in spec.json notes. I also added: the add_progress hop, the Git.polish_url/is_cygwin/check_unsafe_protocols references that are cut, the list-value check, and today's re-run of the end-to-end git check. Flow, slice and commits are unchanged.
analyst.fix_effect_note: The clean commit closes the modelled flow, which uses the default split_single_char_options=True path: the smuggled value becomes a candidate and is rejected as --upload-pack. The fix is deliberately narrow. The joined -nVALUE token used when split_single_char_options=False still gives the candidate ['-n'] at the clean commit; I confirmed this. That path is a separate advisory (GHSA-wvpp, fixed later in 96a888f4) and is not modelled here. The same builder also guards parallel flows that this fix closes too but that are not modelled: Remote.fetch/pull/push, Repo.iter_commits/blame/blame_incremental/archive, Commit.iter_items and Git.ls_remote.
analyst.flow_summary:
1. Entry: git/repo/base.py::Repo.clone_from (library-api). It receives the caller's **kwargs, for example n='--upload-pack=touch X;git-upload-pack', and forwards them unchanged to Repo._clone.
2. Guard: Repo._clone calls Git.check_unsafe_options(options=Git._option_candidates([], kwargs), unsafe_options=Repo.unsafe_git_clone_options).
   - Regressed: git/cmd.py::Git._option_candidates builds candidates from the kwarg keys only and returns ['-n']. That is not on the denylist, and 'n' is a clusterable short flag, so the check passes.
   - Clean: the fix adds the dash-prefixed values of one-letter kwargs whenever split_single_char_options is on (the default), including list and tuple values. So '--upload-pack=...' becomes a candidate, its canonical name 'upload-pack' matches the denylist, and UnsafeOptionError is raised before git runs.
3. Sink: Repo._clone then calls git.clone(multi, '--', url, path, v=True, **add_progress(kwargs, git, progress)).
   - That call goes through Git.__getattr__ to Git._call_process, then Git.transform_kwargs, then Git.transform_kwarg('n', value, True), which returns ['-n', '--upload-pack=...'] as two argv tokens.
   - _call_process then calls self.execute(call). The Popen (safer_popen) inside git/cmd.py::Git.execute starts `git clone -v -n --upload-pack=<cmd> -- url path`. Because -n takes no value, git reads the next token as --upload-pack and runs <cmd>.
   - The slice uses Git._call_process as the sink stand-in, with true_symbol Git.execute.

Checks I ran:
- The real functions taken from both commits gave these results. Regressed lets both n='--upload-pack=...' and n=['--upload-pack=x'] through. Clean blocks both. The harmless n=True, depth=1 and b='main' pass in both.

Two advisories are merged into one event. analyst.fix_effect_note: For the modelled routes, the backslash normalisation before the startswith('/') check rejects the drive-root-relative payload. UNC input (\\host\share) is already rejected at the regressed commit because is_absolute() is True, so the fix only changes the result for the \windows\... form. The fix also edits a second function, sanitize_path, but that change does nothing until bbabf14 because it runs after the startswith('/') check. That hunk is outside the slice and does not appear in regression.diff. Later commits d840831 and 28ee567 deal with separate drive-letter issues and do not affect this flow.
analyst.flow_summary: Entry: an HTTP GET to /user_infos/{path:path}, handled by lollms/server/endpoints/lollms_binding_files_server.py::serve_user_infos. The parallel route /personalities/{path:path} is handled by serve_personalities in the same file. Hop: the handler calls lollms/security.py::sanitize_path_from_endpoint(path) and uses its return value. Guard: at the clean commit (95ad36e) the function runs path.replace('\\', '/') before the startswith('/') check, so \windows\win.ini becomes /windows/win.ini and is rejected with HTTP 400. At the regressed commit (41577f4) there is no normalisation. \windows\win.ini passes every check: it has no leading '/', no '..' or '//', no character on the blocklist, and is_absolute() is False on Windows because it has no drive. Sink: back in the same handler, file_path = personal_user_infos_path / path (or personalities_zoo_path / path) resolves to C:\windows\win.ini, and file_path.exists() is followed by FileResponse(str(file_path)), an arbitrary file read. I verified this by importing both built security.py slices on Windows with fastapi and ascii_colors stubbed out: the regressed slice passes the payload through and the join gives C:\windows\win.ini; the clean slice rejects it.
analyst.scope_evidence: Both the entry and the sink are in lollms/server/endpoints/lollms_binding_files_server.py (serve_user_infos and serve_personalities). The guard, sanitize_path_from_endpoint, is in lollms/security.py, the only file the fix changes. The built event.json has scope=cross_file.

check.class_note: Path-traversal (CWE-22) is correct. A request-controlled path segment escapes the base directory through a pathlib join that resets to the drive root on Windows, and the result is read with FileResponse. The advisories label it CWE-22/CWE-36. Both advisories describe the same root cause: sanitize_path_from_endpoint does not normalise backslashes. They reach it through different routes of the same file (/user_infos and /personalities; /del_preset is in lollms-webui). This is one flaw closed by one guard hunk, so merging them into one event is correct.
check.clean_blocks_note: In the clean slice, sanitize_path_from_endpoint runs path.replace('\\','/') at line 24, before the startswith('/') check. It sits on the same call path for both routes. I ran payloads against the clean slice: '\windows\win.ini' becomes '/windows/win.ini' and is rejected with 400 'Invalid path!'. ' \windows\win.ini' is rejected by the strip().startswith check, '\\host\share' is rejected, and 'a\\windows' becomes 'a//windows' and is rejected by the '//' pattern. The regressed slice already rejects UNC input, so the fix changes the outcome specifically for the drive-root-relative form. That form is the flow modelled here, and the clean slice closes it. The later drive-letter issues (d840831 removing ':' from the blocklist, fixed by 28ee567) are separate and do not affect this flow at the clean commit, where ':' is still blocklisted.

analyst.class_note: The advisory labels this CWE-77 ('command'), but the code never runs a shell or an OS command. The request field `name` is used as a directory path. A name containing '..', or an absolute path, escapes bindings_zoo_path, and SourceFileLoader then loads and runs <path>/__init__.py. That is CWE-22 path traversal leading to code execution (CWE-94). The fix is a path sanitizer (sanitize_path), which supports this reading. Both 2.2 reviewers read it the same way.
concerns: The class is relabelled from the advisory's command/CWE-77 to path-traversal, based on the code (traversal into an importlib module load). The project owner should confirm.

The model-visible security.py contains the string 'Detected an attempt of path traversal. Are you kidding me?'. It is real behaviour, but it names the weakness in plain words, and it appears in both slices.

Exploiting this requires an attacker-planted __init__.py at the traversed location, supplied by some other write primitive. The dataset flow is request field to module load, which is demonstrable within the repo.

Fix hunks deliberately left out of the slice: install_binding (already guarded by sanitize_path_from_endpoint at the vulnerable commit), reload_binding (os.path.basename already stripped traversal) and lollms_extensions_infos.py::reinstall_extension (the value comes from config, not the request). All three are hardening, and regression.diff contains only the import line and the two modelled assignments.
The guard's effectiveness depends on `raise <str>` producing a TypeError. A model or gate reading the clean slice may see this as a bug rather than as validation.
Known residual: getBinding accepts relative names containing '/' without '..' (resolved against the working directory), and sanitize_path lets them through.
analyst.fix_effect_note: Checked at both commits. binding.py and security.py are byte-identical between b0da52f5 and 7ebe08da; only lollms_binding_infos.py and lollms_extensions_infos.py change. At the clean commit, sanitize_path does `raise exception_text`, which raises a str. In Python 3 that is a TypeError, but it still aborts before build_binding and is caught by the endpoint's except, so '..' and absolute-path names never reach the module load. analyst.flow_summary: Entry: POST /unInstall_binding, lollms/server/endpoints/lollms_binding_infos.py::unInstall_binding. The JSON field `name` (BindingInstallParams, a pydantic str of 1-50 chars with no content check) is assigned to lollmsElfServer.config.binding_name. Sink: getBinding builds the path as Path(config.binding_name) if the name contains '/', otherwise bindings_zoo_path / name. It then calls resolve() and importlib.machinery.SourceFileLoader(module_name, <path>/__init__.py).load_module(), which runs code from the traversed location (e.g. name '../../../../tmp/x'). Guard (clean commit): unInstall_binding assigns sanitize_path(data.name) instead of data.name. sanitize_path (lollms/security.py, unchanged by the fix) raises on '..' or an absolute path inside the try block, before build_binding runs, so the endpoint returns status False. reinstall_binding gets the same one-line fix and is included in the slice as a parallel flow.

check.class_note: path-traversal is correct. No shell and no OS command is invoked. User input becomes a filesystem path that escapes bindings_zoo_path through '..' or an absolute path, and the module at that path is then loaded. That is CWE-22 leading to CWE-94. The advisory's CWE-77 label does not fit the code. The fix is a path sanitizer, which supports this reading. The project owner should confirm the relabel from the advisory's 'command' class.
check.clean_blocks_note: In clean/, unInstall_binding and reinstall_binding assign sanitize_path(data.name), and they do it inside the try block before build_binding runs. I checked in Python that this raises TypeError ('exceptions must derive from BaseException'), which aborts the request before build_binding runs. The endpoint's `except Exception` catches it and returns status False. security.py and binding.py are byte-identical between the two commits: git diff --stat lists only lollms_binding_infos.py and lollms_extensions_infos.py. The modelled flow is closed. A known residual remains: a relative name with '/' but no '..' is resolved against the working directory. The dossier records it, and it is outside the advisory's traversal.

analyst.class_note: Same as the advisory label (CWE-22). Be aware of one nuance: the modelled flow never leaves the source directory. It is a file path controlled by the input document that reaches a file read without the operator's opt-in (--allow-local-file-access). Mechanically that is closer to CWE-73, external control of file name. The flows through entities and xi:include do escape the directory, but they are not modelled (see concerns).
concerns: Class strength. The modelled sourcecode src= flow closes a missing opt-in check: without --allow-local-file-access, a document can pull in any existing file beside or below its own directory. It does not close an escape from that directory: '../' and absolute paths are refused at both commits. Whether this counts as path traversal (CWE-22) is the owner's call. The advisory and both 2.2 reviewers labelled it path-traversal.

Parallel flows fixed by the same commit are not modelled: (1) element_artwork, which uses the same check_src_file_path and has three urlopen sites; (2) external XML entities, via parser.py::CachingResolver.resolve -> getReferenceRequest -> lxml resolve_filename; (3) <xi:include href>, via writers/base.py::BaseV3Writer.xinclude and check_includes -> lxml tree.xinclude(). With the option set, the regressed commit lets (2) and (3) read any file on the filesystem, while the clean commit confines them to the source directory. That is a true escape from the directory. I did not model them because the file read happens inside lxml, and getReferenceRequest plus cache (about 13 KB) would not fit in the slice.

The scrubber removed only the comment line 'security issues.  See Section 7 ...'. The line before it survives in both slices: "#        prevent <sourcecode src='file:///etc/passwd'> and similar" (clean line 238, regressed line 242). It is quoted RFC 7998 text, but it names a classic sensitive-file example and now ends mid-sentence, so it still hints at the purpose. The comment block also says the rule is about files outside the source directory.

regression.diff is only the inverted fix within the slice: file.py is deleted and preptool.py loses its import and the can_access call in check_src_file_path. The fix's hunks in parser.py, base.py, util/__init__.py and test.py fall outside the slice.

The slice keeps the class-level selectors list and element_contact = element_front_author. element_front_author was added only so that alias is not left dangling; it is not on the flow. Several of prep's calls are inherited from BaseV3Writer in base.py and are not in the slice: xinclude, get_refname_mapping, remove_dtd, dispatch.

The clean slice is 12,220 bytes before the last additions (about 4.3k tokens after). No FAIL or WARN in the final build. The regressed-to-clean commit pair is the advisory's own fix commit (the tag v3.27.0 points at it), so I see no reason to doubt the pair.
analyst.fix_effect_note:
For the modelled flow under default options (option off), the clean commit closes it completely: can_access raises, check_src_file_path returns None, and urlopen is never reached. With the option on, both commits behave the same on this flow, which is intended.

The fix is known to be incomplete elsewhere, at both commits:
- Containment uses path.startswith(dir) with no separator, so a sibling directory whose name starts with the source directory's name passes.
- Symlinks are not resolved.

Neither affects the modelled flow.
analyst.flow_summary:
Entry: xml2rfc/writers/preptool.py::PrepToolWriter.element_sourcecode reads the src attribute of <sourcecode> from the input RFCXML document (e.get('src')), kind file-content. PrepToolWriter.prep reaches this function by dispatching the './/sourcecode' selector.

Hops: check_src_scheme maps a src with no scheme to 'file', then check_src_file_path(e, scheme, netloc, path, ...) is called.

Guard (clean commit): check_src_file_path first calls xml2rfc/util/file.py::can_access(self.options, self.xmlrfc.source, path). Unless options.allow_local_file_access is set, can_access raises FileAccessError. check_src_file_path then calls err and returns None, so src is falsy and nothing is read. The regressed commit has no can_access (the whole of file.py is removed). It checks only containment within the source directory, shell metacharacters and existence, never the option, which defaults to False in base.default_options.

Sink: back in element_sourcecode, urlopen(src).read() reads the file:// URL. The content becomes e.text and is written into the output document.

Verified by running the extracted check logic from each commit against a temp directory, with src='secret.txt' placed beside the source file:
- Option off: the regressed commit returns a file: URL; the clean commit refuses.
- '../../etc/passwd': refused at both commits, whether the option is on or off.
- Option on, 'secret.txt': allowed at both commits.

Guard at the clean commit: xinclude always calls check_includes(). check_includes passes every local or file: href to xml2rfc/util/file.py::can_access(self.options, self.xmlrfc.source, href.path). With the option on, can_access does four things in order: it rejects shell metacharacters, resolves the path against the source file's directory, raises FileAccessError unless the result starts with that directory, and requires the file to exist. check_includes then calls die(), which raises RfcWriterError before tree.xinclude() runs.

Regressed commit: xinclude calls check_includes() only `if not self.options.allow_local_file_access`, and file.py does not exist. With the option on, no href is checked.

Sink: BaseV3Writer.xinclude, self.tree.xinclude(). lxml loads each href and splices the file's content into the document, which is written to the output.

exclusion.note:
I checked the code at the clean commit 73fb1c91, and it confirms the analyst's reading.

1. **What the fix commit does.** It changes three files:
   - It adds `XmlRfc.sanitize()` in parser.py (lines 759-762), which calls `strip_link_attachments(self.tree)`.
   - It adds one call, `xmlrfc.sanitize()`, in run.py::main at line 581. That call runs on the object from the first `parser.parse(...)` at line 518.
   - It deletes the `strip_link_attachments(self.tree)` call from `BaseV3Writer.validate` in writers/base.py.

2. **The PDF path never gets the sanitized tree.** The `if options.pdf:` branch (run.py 755-769) starts by assigning `xmlrfc = parser.parse(remove_comments=False, quiet=True, add_xmlns=True)`. `XmlRfcParser.parse` (parser.py 531 onward) re-runs `lxml.etree.iterparse` over the raw bytes in `self.text` and returns a new XmlRfc. The tree passed to `xml2rfc.PdfWriter(xmlrfc, ...)` at line 767 has therefore never been sanitized.

3. **Nothing else strips links on that path.** `PdfWriter.pdf` (writers/pdf.py 60-77) only runs PrepToolWriter when `prepTime` is missing. It then renders `HtmlWriter(...).html()` and calls `weasyprint.HTML(string=html, base_url="")`. At the clean commit, `git grep` finds `strip_link_attachments` only in the utils.py definition and inside `sanitize()`. Its call in validate is gone, so on this path nothing strips `<link rel="attachment">`, whether or not the input is prepped.

4. **The pair is inverted for non-prepped input.** The "regressed" commit e14cd440 still strips links inside prep/validate, so for that input it is safer than the "clean" commit.

The guard (`XmlRfc.sanitize` and its call in run.py) does not sit on the entry-to-sink flow. That flow runs from the CLI input file, re-parsed in run.py::main, to `writers/pdf.py::PdfWriter.pdf`, where `weasyprint.HTML(...)` reads the file. Since the clean side leaves that flow open, it cannot serve as ground truth.

The analyst also says the sanitized object only reaches writers with no file-read sink (legacy html, raw, legacy text, nroff). I did not check that separately, and it does not change the verdict. The verdict depends only on the PDF sink, which is the one the advisory describes.

Two hops are dynamic dispatch that a plain call graph will not resolve. BaseV3Writer.dispatch calls validate_before through getattr on a selector string ('.;validate_before()', built with slugify). The taint carrier is an XML element moved between trees (head.append(link)) rather than a value passed as an argument, and the guard works by mutating a shared tree (it removes nodes). Value-based taint engines may not model either.

The earlier reviewers named HtmlWriter.render_link as the copy point. At b4f349fa the <rfc>-level links, the only place the v3 schema allows <link>, are moved into the head by render_rfc, so render_link is not on this path and was left out of the slice.

analyst.flow_summary:
Regressed b4f349fa. The untrusted RFCXML input file is parsed by parser.py::XmlRfcParser.parse (true_symbol) and reaches the writer through base.py::BaseV3Writer.__init__ as self.tree = xmlrfc.tree (entry, kind file-content). It can contain <rfc><link rel="attachment" href="/etc/passwd"/>.

Hop by hop:
- pdf.py::PdfWriter.pdf: the input has no prepTime, so it runs PrepToolWriter.prep.
- preptool.py::PrepToolWriter.prep runs xinclude, then BaseV3Writer.dispatch(selectors).
- dispatch runs the selector '.;validate_before()'. It builds the method name with slugify and calls it through getattr.
- BaseV3Writer.validate_before calls PrepToolWriter.validate, which calls BaseV3Writer.validate. At the regressed commit this only checks the schema.
- Back in PdfWriter.pdf, HtmlWriter(self.xmlrfc).html() calls html_tree. The shared tree now has prepTime, so it is not prepped a second time.
- html_tree calls render, which calls render_rfc through getattr. render_rfc moves each <rfc>/<link> element verbatim into the HTML <head> with head.append(link).
- The HTML string passes through flatten_unicode_spans into weasyprint.HTML(string=html, base_url="").write_pdf(...). WeasyPrint's default URL fetcher then opens the attachment href and embeds that file in the PDF (sink PdfWriter.pdf, kind filesystem).

Clean f2b245bc: BaseV3Writer.validate first calls the new utils.py::strip_link_attachments(self.tree). This removes every //link[@rel="attachment"] from the shared tree (the prep tool changes xmlrfc.tree in place), so render_rfc never copies the element into the HTML. That closes the flow for unprepped input.

The fix is known to be incomplete. Input that already has prepTime skips the prep tool and therefore skips validate. That bypass is GHSA-9mv7 / CVE-2025-11059, fixed in 73fb1c91 (event xml2rfc-9mv7). The modelled flow is the unprepped-input path, which this commit does close.

At the clean commit, a '..' traversal cannot reach get_range_response: after resolve(), is_relative_to(local_dir) rejects any path outside the directory, including percent-encoded '..' analyst.flow_summary: Entry: an HTTP request to '<url_path>/{filename:path}' (for example /media/%2e%2e/.env) reaches the nested handler read_item, which App.add_media_files registers in nicegui/app/app.py. In the regressed code, read_item builds filepath = Path(local_directory) / filename and checks only filepath.is_file(), with no containment check. It passes the path to get_range_response in nicegui/app/range_response.py, which calls file.stat(). Its nested content_reader then does open(file, 'rb') and streams the bytes back, so any readable file on the server can be downloaded. The guard is in the clean read_item: it resolves local_dir and (local_dir / filename), then returns 404 unless filepath.is_relative_to(local_dir), which closes the flow.
analyst.scope_evidence: The entry and the guard are both in nicegui/app/app.py::App.add_media_files; they share one symbol because read_item is a closure inside it. check.class_note: The class is correct. This is arbitrary file read through '..' or an absolute path in a URL path parameter, which is path traversal (CWE-22) as the advisory states.
check.clean_blocks_note: The clean read_item is the same path with the guard applied. It sets local_dir = Path(local_directory).resolve() and filepath = (local_dir / filename).resolve(), and raises 404 unless filepath.is_relative_to(local_dir) and is_file(). I traced three payloads by hand. (1) GET /media/%2e%2e/.env gives filename '../.env'. After resolve() the path is the parent directory's .env, which is not relative to local_dir, so the response is 404 and get_range_response is never reached. (2) An absolute path such as filename '/etc/passwd': local_dir / '/etc/passwd' becomes /etc/passwd, which is not relative to local_dir, so 404. (3) A symlink inside the directory that points outside: resolve() follows it, so it is rejected too. Upstream history shows no follow-up change or revert of this check (per the 2.2 review, and consistent with the fix.patch).

analyst.flow_summary: Entry: nicegui/elements/upload.py::Upload.__init__. Its nested POST route upload_route reads the multipart form and passes each Starlette UploadFile, whose .filename the client controls, to create_file_upload. Guard: nicegui/elements/upload_files.py::create_file_upload sets the FileUpload name. At the regressed commit it uses PurePosixPath(filename).name, which splits on '/' only, so '..\..\secret\evil.txt' comes through unchanged. analyst.flow_summary: Regressed 67abdbd: the framework passes the request path (share prefix stripped, e.g. /users/<key>) to MySQLBrowserProvider.get_resource_inst. That calls exists(path, environ). _split_path uses util.save_split to split the path into (tableName, primKey). tableName is checked against _list_tables (SHOW TABLES); primKey is not checked at all. _exists_record_by_primary_key(conn, tableName, primKey) then builds "SELECT pk FROM db.table WHERE pk = '" + key + "'" (or the unquoted numeric branch chosen by _is_data_type_numeric, whose INTT typo sends INT keys to the quoted branch) and runs it with cursor.execute (the sink). The found/not-found result sets the response status, which gives a boolean oracle. Clean 6f35776: in the same function the guard is a parameterized query, "SELECT `pk` FROM `db`.`table` WHERE `pk` = %s" with identifiers quoted by _escape_id and cursor.execute(sql, (pri_key_value,)). check.clean_blocks_note: Clean _exists_record_by_primary_key is byte-identical to the real function at 6f35776. It sits on the same path, reached from exists. Test payload: the key 0' OR '1'='1. In the regressed code it builds WHERE id = '0' OR '1'='1', which is always true, so the request gets the found status. That is defence in depth: table_name is already checked against SHOW TABLES and pri_key comes from DESCRIBE.

concerns: The scrubber missed a revealing comment in the clean slice (clean/wsgidav/fs_dav_provider.py, in _loc_to_file_path). The fix added a 3-line comment: 'Ensure the containment check is path-boundary-aware ... a sibling directory (e.g. /tmp/share_evil) whose name *starts with* root_path (/tmp/share) is correctly rejected.' None of its words match the REVEALING regex in src/graphgate/dataset/scrub.py ('evil', 'containment', 'rejected' are not listed), so it was kept (scrubbed 0+0). It explains the guard's purpose and names an attack-style example path, and it sits in the file the model sees. regression.diff removes it, so the diff also carries it. It cannot be removed from spec.json. Suggest adding a pattern such as 'evil|containment' to the scrubber, or a per-event scrub override, and rebuilding.

The error-message literal also differs between commits: the clean version adds '{root_path}' to the message. That makes a tiny extra hunk in regression.diff, but it is part of the real fix commit, not an unrelated change.

Exploitability depends on a sibling directory existing next to the share root whose name starts with the root's basename. The request also has to carry an encoded dot segment (%2e%2e) that the WSGI server decodes into PATH_INFO: WsgiDAVApp.__call__ and RequestServer do no '..' normalisation, and clients normalise a literal '../'. That decoding happens outside the repo's code. The in-repo flow from PATH_INFO to open is fully visible.
Only the GET path is modelled. The same guard also protects PUT, DELETE, MKCOL, PROPFIND/PROPPATCH and the COPY/MOVE Destination paths (copy_move_single / move_recursive); these are not in the slice.
The shadow_map branch (is_shadow) skips the check at both commits by design; it is configuration-controlled.

analyst.flow_summary: HTTP GET: RequestServer.do_GET -> RequestServer._send_resource (wsgidav/request_server.py) reads environ['PATH_INFO'] (e.g. '/../share_evil/secret' after WsgiDAVApp strips the share prefix) -> FilesystemProvider.get_resource_inst -> FilesystemProvider._loc_to_file_path (wsgidav/fs_dav_provider.py) resolves os.path.abspath(join(root, *parts)). The guard is here: at the regressed commit it is file_path.startswith(root_path), which accepts the sibling /tmp/share_evil/secret for root /tmp/share; at the clean commit it compares separator-terminated paths and raises RuntimeError. -> FileResource(path, environ, fp) -> FileResource.get_content open(fp, 'rb'), whose bytes _send_resource streams to the client.

check.regressed_flow_note:
Every hop is visible in regressed/. RequestServer.do_GET calls _send_resource, which reads environ['PATH_INFO'] (request_server.py:85) and calls self._davProvider.get_resource_inst(path, environ) (:86). FilesystemProvider.get_resource_inst calls _loc_to_file_path, which does os.path.abspath(os.path.join(root_path, *path_parts)) and then checks only file_path.startswith(root_path). It returns FileResource(path, environ, fp), and _send_resource calls res.get_content() (:203), which is open(self._file_path, 'rb') streamed to the client.

Attacker control is confirmed in the repo at 593a3b3. WsgiDAVApp.__call__ (wsgidav_app.py:422-467) only re-encodes PATH_INFO, optionally unquotes it and strips the share prefix. It does no '..' normalisation, and line 459 still carries the upstream TODO about URLs containing '..'. RequestResolver passes PATH_INFO through untouched. There is no normpath or '..' filter anywhere under wsgidav/.

Running the slice expressions with root /tmp/share: '/../share_evil/secret' resolves to /tmp/share_evil/secret and the regressed check passes it.

Caveat, already noted by the analyst: a '..' segment only reaches PATH_INFO if the WSGI server decodes %2e%2e without collapsing it, and the escape reaches only sibling directories whose name starts with the root's basename.

revealing_text_left.text: # Ensure the containment check is path-boundary-aware: append os.sep so / that a sibling directory (e.g. /tmp/share_evil) whose name *starts with* / root_path (/tmp/share) is correctly rejected.  (lines 133-135; also appears as removed lines in regression.diff)
f"Security exception: tried to access file outside root {root_path}: {file_path}"  (runtime message, present at both commits; regressed line 135 has the same wording without {root_path})

concerns: The flow is exploitable only on Windows and only with a leading backslash (optionally after a leading '/'). On POSIX a backslash is a literal filename character and os.path.isfile fails. The code is platform-independent Python, but a gate reasoning about POSIX semantics could fairly call the regressed code safe.

The regression is two one-line changes that each remove a .replace('\\', '/') call. The '..' check in Template.__init__ is still present in the regressed code, so this is a weakened guard, not a removed one. Graph rules keyed on a guard node or edge disappearing (R1/R3) may see no structural change; this is a hard case for every gate.
The entry is a library API. Mako has no HTTP layer, so whether the uri is attacker-controlled depends on the embedding application. No request source exists inside the repo.

The scrubber removed one harmless docstring paragraph in mako/lookup.py, in both variants: the modulename_callable parameter description, which uses the word 'inject' about module locations. It is a false positive and unrelated to the flow.
The kept error-message string 'it cannot be relative outside of the root path' is real behaviour and present in both variants. The build did not flag it, but it does hint at the check's purpose.
The clean slice is 22.9 KB (about 6542 tokens), under the 24 KB soft limit. About 8 KB of mako/template.py is the Template class docstring, which 'Class.method' slicing always keeps.
TemplateLookup's base class TemplateCollection is cut, so the sliced lookup.py references an undefined name at class-definition time. The slice parses but would not import as is.

analyst.fix_effect_note:
The backslash flow is closed at the clean commit, confirmed by running both commits. The Template.__init__ line is what closes it. The lookup.py line alone would not: ntpath.normpath of the unconverted uri still passes the check.

A sibling flow from the same posixpath/ntpath mismatch is still open at the clean commit: the drive-designator uri (e.g. C:/../../x, upstream issue #441, fixed later in 000ed85, per the 2.2 reviewers). It is a separate advisory and is not modelled here.
analyst.flow_summary:
Entry: mako/lookup.py::TemplateLookup.get_template(uri), a public library API taking the template name. On a cache miss, the regressed code strips only leading '/' and builds srcfile = posixpath.normpath(posixpath.join(dir_, u)). posixpath treats a backslash as an ordinary character, so the '..' segments survive. os.path.isfile(srcfile) then resolves them on Windows, and the hit goes to TemplateLookup._load(srcfile, uri), which constructs Template(uri=uri, filename=...).

Guard: mako/template.py::Template.__init__ computes u_norm = os.path.normpath(self.uri.lstrip('/')) and raises TemplateLookupException if it starts with '..'. In the regressed code a leading-backslash uri normalises to '\secrets\creds.txt' on Windows, so the check passes. The flow continues to Template._compile_from_file and then the sink, mako/util.py::read_file (open(path).read()). The content is compiled by _compile_text and returned by render().

The clean commit adds .replace('\\', '/') in both get_template and Template.__init__. u_norm becomes '../../...' and the exception is raised before any read.

I ran both commits' mako package on Windows (Python 3.12):
- '\..\..\secrets\creds.txt' and '/\..\..\secrets\creds.txt' return the outside file's content at 4ae11bd and raise TemplateLookupException at 72e10c5.
- '..\..\secrets\creds.txt' and '/../../secrets/creds.txt' are rejected at both commits.
- 'index.html' loads at both.
analyst.scope_evidence:
Copied from the built event.json (scope=cross_file; flow_files are mako/lookup.py, mako/template.py, mako/util.py).
- Entry: mako/lookup.py (TemplateLookup.get_template).
- Effective guard: mako/template.py (Template.__init__, the u_norm startswith('..') check). A companion guard line is in mako/lookup.py (get_template).
- Sink: mako/util.py (read_file, the real open() call, small enough to be in the slice, so no true_symbol stand-in).
The regression changes both lookup.py and template.py. The label would still be cross_file if the sink were taken as the os.path.isfile probe in lookup.py, because the rejecting guard is in template.py.

analyst.flow_summary: Entry: mako/lookup.py::TemplateLookup.get_template(uri) (library-api; uri is typically derived from a request path). Modelled flow: a LIKE-family filter value on the MySQL backend.

- Entry: tortoise/queryset.py::QuerySet.filter(**kwargs) (library-api), e.g. filter(name__contains=<text>). QuerySet._filter_or_exclude wraps each key/value in a Q.
- Hops on await: QuerySet.__await__ -> QuerySet._make_query -> AwaitableQuery.resolve_filters -> tortoise/query_utils.py::Q.resolve -> Q._resolve_kwargs -> Q._get_actual_filter_params (checks the key only) -> Q._resolve_regular_kwarg -> _process_filter_kwarg.

- Guard: tortoise/backends/mysql/executor.py::mysql_contains.
  - Regressed: Cast(field, CHAR).like(f"%{value}%"). pypika's stock ValueWrapper only doubles single quotes, so the value \' renders as \'' and the rest of the value becomes SQL under MySQL's default backslash escapes.
  - Clean: Like(Cast(...), StrWrapper(f"%{escape_like(value)}%"), escape=""). escape_like turns each backslash into four and escapes % and _; StrWrapper doubles quotes. Breakout is closed.
- Sink: QuerySet._execute -> tortoise/backends/base/executor.py::BaseExecutor.execute_select -> self.db.execute_query(query.get_sql()) -> tortoise/backends/mysql/client.py::MySQLClient.execute_query -> cursor.execute(query, None).

By reading, not execution: the guard is on the same path and closes the payload.

- Same path: FILTER_FUNC_OVERRIDE still maps `contains` to mysql_contains; the five unchanged files are byte-identical between clean/ and regressed/.
- Payload: value = \' OR 1=1 --  (backslash, quote, then SQL).
  - Regressed renders '%\'' OR 1=1 -- %'. MySQL reads \' as an escaped quote, the next quote ends the literal, and OR 1=1 runs as SQL.
  - Clean: escape_like turns the backslash into four, StrWrapper doubles the quote, giving '%\\\\'' OR 1=1 -- %'. MySQL reads two escaped backslashes, then '' as a literal quote; the string does not terminate.
- The same holds for mysql_starts_with, mysql_ends_with and the three insensitive LIKE variants.
- Depends on pypika passing secondary_quote_char="'" into get_value_sql (its ValueWrapper.get_sql default). If it did not, StrWrapper would emit no quotes at all. I could not check this against pypika source.
- mysql_insensitive_exact is not closed inside the clean slice: it still uses pypika's ValueWrapper and relies on the get_value_sql monkey-patch, which is cut. It is closed in the real clean commit. This is a parallel flow, not the recorded one.

check.diff_note:
Every hunk in regression.diff is part of the inverted fix 91c3640; no unrelated hunks. The mysql/executor.py part matches the real reverse diff. Two caveats:

- It is a subset: the filters.py get_value_sql monkey-patch, its assignment over ValueWrapper.get_value_sql, and escape_val are cut, so the diff shows an import-only hunk in filters.py (Enum, basestring, date, format_quotes) with no visible user.

check.regressed_flow_note:
Traceable in regressed/, with one hop that is data-driven and only half visible.

- Visible chain: QuerySet.filter -> _filter_or_exclude (wraps value in Q) -> __await__ -> _make_query -> AwaitableQuery.resolve_filters -> Q.resolve -> _resolve_kwargs -> _get_actual_filter_params (checks the key only) -> _resolve_regular_kwarg -> _process_filter_kwarg -> param["value_encoder"] / param["operator"](column, value).
- Operator swap: MetaInfo._generate_filters + BaseExecutor.get_overridden_filter_func + MySQLExecutor.FILTER_FUNC_OVERRIDE send `contains` to mysql_contains, which builds Cast(field, CHAR).like(f"%{value}%").
- Sink: QuerySet._execute -> BaseExecutor.execute_select -> self.db.execute_query(query.get_sql()) -> MySQLClient.execute_query -> cursor.execute(query, None).
- Not visible: what binds the key "<field>__contains" to the operator `contains` and the encoder `string_encoder`. That table is filters.py::get_filters_for_field, which is cut (models.py still imports it). I confirmed it in the repo at the regressed commit (tortoise/filters.py lines 253-258).
- Attacker control: the value is a caller-supplied argument to a public library API (Model.filter at models.py:885 delegates to QuerySet.filter). The only transformation before the operator is str(value). The client sets sql_mode to STRICT_TRANS_TABLES only, so MySQL backslash escapes stay on.
- Not verified by me either: that stock pypika ValueWrapper only doubles quotes. pypika is not installed here and is not in the clone. It is consistent with the fix's replacement get_value_sql (pypika's function plus one MySQL backslash line), the requirements pin pypika>=0.36.1, and the fix's own test strings (tests/test_fuzz.py includes "a\\'").

Entry kind is library-api: ormar is an ORM library, and no HTTP handler exists in the repo. The advisory's exploit assumes an application forwards a request parameter to Model.objects.max(column).

The clean check is a field-name membership test, not parameterisation: the sink still uses sqlalchemy.text() at the clean commit. A taint tool that does not model the membership check as a sanitiser may flag both variants.
Fix effect was established by code reading at both commits, not by running the upstream tests or a proof of concept.

The Query class behind build_select_expression (ormar/queryset/queries/query.py) and the database executor are not in the slice; neither carries the column string. The build reported no dropped references.
analyst.fix_effect_note: Verified by reading both commits; I did not execute the code. At the clean commit field_name must be a key of target_model.model_fields (declared field names, which are Python identifiers), so the advisory payloads ('1 + 1', 'category__1 + 1', a sqlite_master subquery) raise QueryDefinitionError before apply_func. SelectAction is constructed only in _query_aggr_function (git grep at the regressed commit), so this one check covers every route to the sink, including QuerysetProxy.min/max. sum/avg were already blocked at both commits because is_numeric indexes model_fields[field_name] and raises KeyError for unknown names. The later upstream change from text() to column() (9b405ab, 0.25.0) is hardening, not part of this pair.
analyst.flow_summary: Entry: ormar/queryset/queryset.py::QuerySet.max (and QuerySet.min) take the caller's column string, wrap it in a list and pass it to QuerySet._query_aggr_function(func_name, columns). There, SelectAction(select_str=column, model_cls=self.model) is built for each column. QueryAction.__init__ (ormar/queryset/actions/query_action.py) calls SelectAction._split_value_into_parts (ormar/queryset/actions/select_action.py), which sets field_name to the last '__' segment and related_parts to the rest, then _determine_filter_target_table -> get_relationship_alias_model_and_str (ormar/queryset/utils.py), which resolves target_model and table_prefix (relation segments must already be real fields at both commits). Back in _query_aggr_function, x.apply_func(func) calls SelectAction.get_text_clause, the sink: sqlalchemy.text(f"{alias}{self.field_name}") makes the string literal SQL, wrapped in func.max/min. _query_aggr_function then builds sqlalchemy.select(*select_columns) and runs it with executor.fetch_one(expr). Guard (clean only, in QuerySet._query_aggr_function, before apply_func): raises QueryDefinitionError if any x.field_name is not in x.target_model.model_fields. At the regressed commit only sum/avg are checked (is_numeric), so min/max pass any string through to the SQL text.
analyst.scope_evidence: Entry (QuerySet.max/min) and guard (QuerySet._query_aggr_function, the only Python function the fix changes) are in ormar/queryset/queryset.py. The sink, the raw SQL text construction sqlalchemy.text() in SelectAction.get_text_clause, is in ormar/queryset/actions/select_action.py. The tainted field_name is also derived in another file (SelectAction._split_value_into_parts, called from QueryAction.__init__ in query_action.py). The built event.json reports scope=cross_file with flow_files select_action.py and queryset.py. Note the statement is executed back in queryset.py (executor.fetch_one in _query_aggr_function); see concerns.
